assumptions: The bundled feature libraries are the reference set.
Exact match and local alignment under the identity and coverage cutoffs given.
limits: A part absent from the libraries cannot be found; a diverged copy is reported with its identity, not named as exact.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which known parts (vector elements, origins, markers, tags, lox and att sites) does this sequence carry, and where?

description: Find and name known features on the subject — vector parts, origins, resistance markers and tags — by exact match, by local alignment (which finds a diverged copy and reports the identity and coverage that earned it), or by both, on either strand and across the origin, plus Cre/loxP and Gateway att recognition sites. Emits an annotated record, so a downstream map or export carries the annotations.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

accepted_only.description: keep only hits clearing the corpus authority's own acceptance policy (>=95% identity, with a coverage bar that depends on the feature's length). Also decides overlaps: a hit the authority would reject cannot displace one it would accept. Only applies when mode is alignment or both. Advanced.

alternatives.description: protein corpora only: how many runners-up to keep on each call, so a near relative is reported rather than implied. Advanced.

genetic_code.description: protein corpora only: the NCBI translation table the six frames are read under. 1 is the standard code. Advanced.

greedy_gateway.description: permissive att core matching — finds more sites, including partial ones. Only applies when gateway is true. Advanced.

hide_fragments.description: hide hits covering under 95% of their database entry, which upstream calls fragments. Only applies when mode is alignment or both. Advanced.

libraries.description: which feature corpora to search, by id (an id from annotation-library/manifest.json, or "legacy" for the unsourced set). Empty means the ones the panel starts with, which is every corpus but the two it leaves off for their size, AMRFinderPlus and Rfam; name those to search them too.

max_expect.description: protein corpora only: the E-value a translated (six-frame) match must beat to be reported. It also sets the score the search runs at, so a stricter cutoff is a faster scan. Advanced.

min_coverage.description: protein corpora only: drop a translated call covering less than this much of the database protein's own length. Advanced.

min_identity.description: protein corpora only: drop a translated call under this percent identity over the residues aligned. Advanced.

min_pi_per_match.description: lowest identity-weighted coverage worth reporting; upstream's own floor is 3, below which a hit is a fragment of a composite feature rather than the feature. Only applies when mode is alignment or both. Advanced.

mode.description: how to match a library entry: "exact" finds only a sequence spelled byte for byte, "alignment" finds a diverged copy and reports its identity and coverage, "both" runs each and keeps what only the other found.

policy.description: what the emitted record does with the features it already had: `merge` keeps them all and skips a hit already there to the base, `overwrite` replaces a same-strand feature a hit overlaps, `clear` drops every existing feature first.

name: auto_annotate

features.description: every feature found, with its source detector

record.description: the subject with the found features added
